name: Extension presence probing
plain: Detects installed Chrome extensions by fetching their exposed files.
meaning: Learns which extensions the person runs: job tools, ad blockers, accessibility aids, religious or political filters. LinkedIn probes about 6,236 IDs, mapping the result to a named member.

web.api: fetch('chrome-extension://<32-char-id>/<file>') succeeds only if exposed via web_accessible_resources; DOM scanning for injected IDs

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can find out which Chrome extensions you have by testing known files
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads in Chrome or Edge
can: Test thousands of extension IDs one by one (LinkedIn tests about 6,236)
See extensions like ad blockers, job tools, and accessibility aids
Match your list to a named account if you are signed in
Use the list to tell you apart from other visitors
cannot: Work in Firefox, Safari, or on mobile browsers
See extensions that hide their files from sites
See your extension settings or data
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome and Edge are open to this. Firefox, Safari, and mobile browsers are not.

story.what_it_is: Checks which browser extensions you have installed by testing for their hidden files.
story.for_you: You never see it. A page quietly tries to open files that only exist if a specific extension is installed. The result can reveal job tools, ad blockers, accessibility aids and more.
story.for_makers: Extensions say a lot about a person: work, health, beliefs. Some sites use the list to catch scrapers or prohibited tools. It can also be used for profiling, which is why it is controversial and heavily criticised.

use_cases.example: A bot defence checks for known automation extensions to stop scraping.
A professional network scans for extensions that scrape profiles, and bans accounts that use them.
An ad platform tests for ad blocker extensions to decide whether to show a wall or an alternative ad.
A game site detects cheat helper extensions and removes players from ranked modes.
A bank detects remote access or screen sharing extensions that scammers use and shows a warning.
A researcher shows how a site could learn that someone uses a screen reader extension.
A fingerprinting vendor adds the extension list to a stable device ID.

risks: Can reveal work, health or beliefs
Hidden and hard to opt out

technical_bounds: Only works if the extension exposes a resource
Firefox uses random per-install UUIDs; Safari does not expose IDs

abuse: Inferring religion, politics, disability, job search from extensions

linkedin.how: Core of BrowserGate: parallel fetch to chrome-extension URLs for ~6,236 IDs, plus DOM scan; Chrome-family only.

history.change: LinkedIn probe list starts at 38 ids (alleged)
